quests.question: Always wash your hands ____ you sit down to eat.
quests.sentence: Always wash your hands ____ you sit down to eat.
quests.hint: Washing hands should happen first - before eating, not after.
quests.explanation: 'Before' shows that one action must happen earlier than another. Washing hands BEFORE eating is a hygiene rule - 'after' would mean eating first, which defeats the purpose.

quests.question: She felt much better ____ she had a long and restful sleep.
quests.sentence: She felt much better ____ she had a long and restful sleep.
quests.hint: The good sleep came first; feeling better followed.
quests.explanation: 'After' shows that one event follows another. Feeling better (result) came after the restorative sleep (earlier event). 'Before' would reverse the chronology incorrectly.

quests.question: He read his book ____ he was waiting for his appointment.
quests.sentence: He read his book ____ he was waiting for his appointment.
quests.hint: Two things happened at the same time - reading and waiting occurred together.
quests.explanation: 'While' shows two simultaneous activities. He was reading AND waiting at the same time - 'while' connects a background activity (waiting) with a foreground action (reading).

quests.question: They searched every pocket ____ they finally found the missing ticket.
quests.sentence: They searched every pocket ____ they finally found the missing ticket.
quests.hint: The searching continued right up to the point when the ticket was found.
quests.explanation: 'Until' shows duration up to a specific endpoint. They kept searching continuously UNTIL the ticket was found (the stopping point). 'When' would describe a single moment, not the duration.

quests.question: Always proofread your work carefully ____ you press send.
quests.sentence: Always proofread your work carefully ____ you press send.
quests.hint: Proofreading must come first, before the email is sent.
quests.explanation: 'Before' shows prior action. Proofreading should happen BEFORE pressing send - doing it after would be too late. 'After' would reverse this important sequence.

quests.question: She called to say thank you ____ she received the gift.
quests.sentence: She called to say thank you ____ she received the gift.
quests.hint: Receiving the gift came first; the thank-you call came second.
quests.explanation: 'After' places the call after receiving the gift - she received it first, then called. 'Before' would mean she called before even getting the gift, which doesn't make sense.

quests.question: The baby slept peacefully ____ her parents tidied the whole house.
quests.sentence: The baby slept peacefully ____ her parents tidied the whole house.
quests.hint: The baby's sleeping and the tidying happened at the same time.
quests.explanation: 'While' connects two simultaneous events. The baby slept (background state) while the parents tidied (foreground activity) - both happened during the same period.

quests.question: Please wait in the reception area ____ the doctor is ready to see you.
quests.sentence: Please wait in the reception area ____ the doctor is ready to see you.
quests.hint: Waiting continues right up to the moment the doctor is ready.
quests.explanation: 'Until' marks the endpoint of a waiting period. The waiting lasts UNTIL the doctor is ready (the stopping point). At that moment, the waiting ends and the appointment begins.

quests.question: He skipped breakfast ____ he was already running very late.
quests.sentence: He skipped breakfast ____ he was already running very late.
quests.hint: Running late is the reason he skipped breakfast, not a time marker.
quests.explanation: 'Because' gives the reason. Being late (cause) explains skipping breakfast (result). 'While' would imply the two things happened at the same time, which changes the meaning entirely.

quests.question: She applied sunscreen carefully ____ she went out into the sun.
quests.sentence: She applied sunscreen carefully ____ she went out into the sun.
quests.hint: Sunscreen goes on first - before sun exposure, not during or after.
quests.explanation: 'Before' shows prior action. Applying sunscreen BEFORE going out is the correct order - sunscreen needs to be on before UV exposure to protect the skin.

quests.question: He stretched for ten minutes ____ he finished his morning run.
quests.sentence: He stretched for ten minutes ____ he finished his morning run.
quests.hint: Stretching came at the end, after the run was over.
quests.explanation: 'After' places the stretching following the run. He ran first, then stretched. This is the standard cool-down routine. 'Before' would make it a warm-up instead.

quests.question: She read a novel ____ she was waiting for her delayed train.
quests.sentence: She read a novel ____ she was waiting for her delayed train.
quests.hint: Reading and waiting happened at the same time - she passed the time reading.
quests.explanation: 'While' shows two simultaneous activities. She read (activity) while she waited (background condition) - both happened during the same period of delay.

quests.question: He practised the piano every day ____ he could play the piece fluently.
quests.sentence: He practised the piano every day ____ he could play the piece fluently.
quests.hint: Practice continued right up to the point of being able to play fluently.
quests.explanation: 'Until' marks the goal or endpoint. He practised UNTIL he achieved fluency (the stopping condition). The practice continued for as long as needed to reach that standard.

quests.question: She took an umbrella ____ the sky looked very threatening.
quests.sentence: She took an umbrella ____ the sky looked very threatening.
quests.hint: The threatening sky is the direct reason she took an umbrella.
quests.explanation: 'Because' gives the reason for a precautionary action. The threatening sky (cause) explains why she took an umbrella (response). 'While' would suggest both things happened at the same time, not that one caused the other.

quests.question: He always waves ____ he sees a neighbour in the street.
quests.sentence: He always waves ____ he sees a neighbour in the street.
quests.hint: Seeing a neighbour is the regular trigger for waving.
quests.explanation: 'When' connects a regular trigger (seeing a neighbour) to a habitual social action (waving). This happens every time - 'if' would imply he might not see neighbours.

quests.question: They had dessert ____ they finished the main course.
quests.sentence: They had dessert ____ they finished the main course.
quests.hint: The main course came first; dessert followed.
quests.explanation: 'After' shows chronological order. Dessert was eaten AFTER the main course was finished - this is the natural meal sequence. 'Before' would reverse the order.

quests.question: He saved his document ____ he closed his laptop.
quests.sentence: He saved his document ____ he closed his laptop.
quests.hint: Saving first is critical - it must happen before closing.
quests.explanation: 'Before' shows the necessary prior action. Saving must happen BEFORE closing the laptop - doing it after would mean the work might be lost.

quests.question: She kept her phone on silent ____ she was in the cinema.
quests.sentence: She kept her phone on silent ____ she was in the cinema.
quests.hint: Both events happened at the same time - the phone was silent during the film.
quests.explanation: 'While' shows a state that lasted for the duration of an event. The phone was on silent throughout the time she was watching the film.

quests.question: The children played outside ____ it got too dark to see.
quests.sentence: The children played outside ____ it got too dark to see.
quests.hint: They played right up to the moment when darkness stopped them.
quests.explanation: 'Until' marks the natural stopping point. The children played UNTIL it became too dark - the darkness was the endpoint of their outdoor play.

quests.question: You will get a ten-percent discount ____ you show your student card.
quests.sentence: You will get a ten-percent discount ____ you show your student card.
quests.hint: Showing the student card is the condition for getting the discount.
quests.explanation: 'If' introduces a condition. The discount is available IF (and only if) you show the card. 'When' would assume you will definitely show it - 'if' makes it a requirement.

quests.question: She felt an enormous wave of relief ____ she posted the letter.
quests.sentence: She felt an enormous wave of relief ____ she posted the letter.
quests.hint: She posted the letter first; the relief came immediately afterwards.
quests.explanation: 'After' places the relief following the action. She posted the letter (action) and AFTER doing so, she felt relief. The act of posting caused the relief.

quests.question: He always studies the menu carefully ____ he orders.
quests.sentence: He always studies the menu carefully ____ he orders.
quests.hint: Studying the menu happens first, before deciding what to order.
quests.explanation: 'Before' shows prior action. He studies the menu BEFORE ordering - this is the logical sequence: choose what you want before telling the waiter.

quests.question: The little girl splashed in puddles ____ her mother chatted with a friend.
quests.sentence: The little girl splashed in puddles ____ her mother chatted with a friend.
quests.hint: The splashing and the chatting happened simultaneously.
quests.explanation: 'While' connects two simultaneous activities. The girl splashed (her activity) while her mother chatted (her activity) - both happened at the same time in the same place.

quests.question: They talked on the phone ____ one of them finally said goodbye.
quests.sentence: They talked on the phone ____ one of them finally said goodbye.
quests.hint: The conversation continued right up to the goodbye.
quests.explanation: 'Until' marks the endpoint. The conversation lasted UNTIL someone said goodbye (the stopping point). At that moment, the call ended.

quests.question: She returned the dress ____ she discovered it was the wrong size.
quests.sentence: She returned the dress ____ she discovered it was the wrong size.
quests.hint: Discovering the wrong size is the clear reason for returning it.
quests.explanation: 'Because' gives the reason for an action. Finding the wrong size (cause) explains the return (result). 'After' would show timing but not explain why she returned it.

quests.question: Everyone stopped talking ____ the headteacher walked into the hall.
quests.sentence: Everyone stopped talking ____ the headteacher walked into the hall.
quests.hint: The headteacher entering is the specific moment that caused silence.
quests.explanation: 'When' shows that a specific event (the headteacher entering) triggered an immediate response (silence). The moment of arrival is the trigger - 'before' would mean they went quiet before she arrived.

quests.question: He washed all the pots and pans ____ he had cooked a big dinner.
quests.sentence: He washed all the pots and pans ____ he had cooked a big dinner.
quests.hint: Cooking happened first; washing up came afterwards.
quests.explanation: 'After' shows the chronological order. He cooked first (main activity), then washed up (second activity). 'Before' would mean he cleaned the pots before using them to cook.

quests.question: She prepared her slides ____ her colleagues were having lunch.
quests.sentence: She prepared her slides ____ her colleagues were having lunch.
quests.hint: Preparing and lunching happened at the same time.
quests.explanation: 'While' shows two simultaneous activities happening at the same time. She worked on her slides during the same period her colleagues were at lunch.

quests.question: She didn't feel confident about driving ____ she had completed several lessons.
quests.sentence: She didn't feel confident about driving ____ she had completed several lessons.
quests.hint: Confidence only arrived after multiple lessons - right up to that point.
quests.explanation: 'Until' marks the endpoint of a state. She lacked confidence UNTIL the lessons gave her the skill. The lessons were the turning point - before them, no confidence; after them, confidence.

quests.question: Always read the instructions carefully ____ you start assembling the furniture.
quests.sentence: Always read the instructions carefully ____ you start assembling the furniture.
quests.hint: Reading first prevents mistakes - it must come before starting.
quests.explanation: 'Before' shows the necessary prior action. Instructions should be read BEFORE starting - reading them after you've assembled something incorrectly is useless.
